title: FedPEFT-IMU — Experimental Results

dataset.name: harbox
dataset.description: crowd-sourced smartphone IMU, 9 axes, 77 phone models

encoders.name: limu_bert
encoders.pretrained_source: Official LIMU-BERT weights pretrained on HHAR (phones + smartwatches)

encoders.name: ssl_wearables
encoders.pretrained_source: Official Oxford harnet10 weights, self-supervised on UK-Biobank wrist data

encoders.name: unimts
encoders.architecture: ST-GCN, 10 graph blocks over a 22-joint skeleton, 64-512 channels
encoders.pretrained_source: Official UniMTS weights (motion-capture-synthesised IMU aligned with text)

encoders.name: halo
encoders.architecture: Patch-channel Transformer, 8 alternating temporal/channel layers, d=192
encoders.pretrained_source: Our re-implementation, self-supervised (MAE + patch contrastive) on the pool users

encoders.name: mlp
encoders.architecture: Flatten + one fully connected layer (300 units), as in ClusterFL / FedCHAR

methods.name: fedavg_scratch
methods.label: FedAvg from scratch
methods.description: Random initialisation; the whole model is trained and uploaded every round.

methods.name: v0_full_ft
methods.label: V0 · Full fine-tuning
methods.description: Pretrained encoder; the whole model is fine-tuned and uploaded (upper-cost baseline).

methods.name: v1_head_only
methods.label: V1 · Head only
methods.description: Frozen pretrained encoder; only the heads g and h are trained and uploaded (lower-cost baseline).

methods.name: v2_lora_naive
methods.label: V2 · LoRA, naive avg
methods.description: LoRA (r=8) + heads; the server averages A and B separately: avg(B)·avg(A).

methods.name: v3_lora_exact
methods.label: V3 · LoRA, exact avg
methods.description: LoRA (r=8) + heads; exact FedEx-LoRA aggregation avg(B·A), residual folded into W0.

methods.name: v4_hetero_rank
methods.label: V4 · Heterogeneous ranks
methods.description: Device tiers train LoRA ranks 2/4/8; zero-pad, exact aggregation, SVD re-factorisation.

methods.name: v5_proposed
methods.label: V5 · FedPEFT-IMU (proposed)
methods.description: V4 + local norm + local input adapter + personal head + class-prototype alignment.

methods.name: v5_abl_no_local_norm
methods.label: V5 without local norm and input adapter
methods.description: V5, but the normalisation layers and the input adapter stay frozen (only the classifier is personal).

methods.name: v5_abl_shared_head
methods.label: V5 with a shared classifier
methods.description: V5, but the classifier is federated (shared) instead of personal; norm and adapter stay local.

methods.name: v5_abl_fixed_rank
methods.label: V5 with one LoRA rank (r = 8) on every device
methods.description: V5 without device tiers: every client trains rank 8 (exact aggregation + SVD as in V5).

methods.name: local_scratch
methods.label: Local training (no FL)
methods.description: Every client trains its own model from scratch on its own data; nothing is shared.

methods.name: ditto_scratch
methods.label: Ditto (personalised FL)
methods.description: Ditto (Li et al., ICML 2021), the basis of FedCHAR: a global FedAvg model plus a personal model per client, trained with a proximal term towards the global model.

methods.name: ditto_ft
methods.label: Ditto on the pretrained encoder
methods.description: Ditto starting from the pretrained encoder (V0 + a personal model per client): the strongest personalised full-model baseline, with the communication cost of V0.

rows.method: V5 · FedPEFT-IMU (proposed), LoRA on all layers

findings: Under the published protocol, our best federated model (Ditto-FT, LIMU-BERT) reaches a mean user accuracy of 0.950, against 0.917 for the best published federated result (FedCHAR, IMWUT 2023, Tab. 4). Purely local training without any federation already reaches 0.878 under this protocol, consistent with the train/test overlap of its random split. Our re-run of the published FedAvg + MLP baseline scores 0.797 (published 0.694).

Centralized from scratch, LIMU-BERT is the strongest architecture (macro-F1 0.847). Starting from the pretrained weights changes the macro-F1 of each encoder by: LIMU-BERT -0.018, ssl-wearables +0.017, UniMTS +0.024, HALO +0.125 macro-F1.

Training from scratch in the federation (non-IID users, 20 % participation) loses LIMU-BERT 0.058, ssl-wearables 0.050, UniMTS 0.082, HALO 0.130, MLP 0.045 macro-F1 against centralized training from scratch. This is the gap the pretrained encoders are meant to close.

FedPEFT-IMU (V5) against full fine-tuning (V0), macro-F1: LIMU-BERT 0.863 vs 0.801 with 8x less uplink; ssl-wearables 0.879 vs 0.817 with 52x less uplink; UniMTS 0.827 vs 0.811 with 38x less uplink; HALO 0.813 vs 0.716 with 95x less uplink.

Federated LoRA without personalisation (best of V2/V3) against V0: LIMU-BERT V3 0.767 vs V0 0.801; ssl-wearables V3 0.828 vs V0 0.817; UniMTS V3 0.814 vs V0 0.811; HALO V3 0.699 vs V0 0.716. LoRA matches or beats full fine-tuning for ssl-wearables, UniMTS; for LIMU-BERT, HALO the frozen features need more than a low-rank update in this round budget.

Exact LoRA aggregation (V3) versus naive averaging (V2), macro-F1 difference: LIMU-BERT +0.000, ssl-wearables +0.004, UniMTS +0.007, HALO +0.001. On average the two rules are within 0.01 macro-F1 here: the naive error is small (see the aggregation-error chart). Exact aggregation must ship the dense residual to every client: downlink per round is LIMU-BERT 2x, ssl-wearables 34x, UniMTS 23x, HALO 10x that of V2.
LoRA rank (LIMU-BERT, V3): r=2 0.745, r=4 0.762, r=8 0.767, r=16 0.783. The best rank is r=16 at 0.04 MB per client-round.
Highest worst-10 % client F1 per encoder: LIMU-BERT Ditto-FT 0.543 (V5 0.510); ssl-wearables V5 0.531; UniMTS V5 0.283; HALO V5 0.381; MLP Local 0.511.

New users, zero-shot (V5 = nearest global prototype; BatchNorm encoders first estimate their norm statistics from the new user's unlabelled windows): LIMU-BERT V5 0.591 vs V3 0.675; ssl-wearables V5 0.775 vs V3 0.788; UniMTS V5 0.715 vs V3 0.762; HALO V5 0.534 vs V3 0.527. On average the shared classifier of V3 transfers better to brand-new users than V5's prototype rule (-0.034); V5's advantage is on the devices that trained with it.

Transductive zero-shot (V5's prototypes first refined on the new user's unlabelled windows, no labels and no communication): LIMU-BERT 0.591 -> 0.626; ssl-wearables 0.775 -> 0.776; UniMTS 0.715 -> 0.732; HALO 0.534 -> 0.554.
Budget note: ssl-wearables, HALO, UniMTS ran with a reduced compute budget (see the callouts), so compare its methods with each other.
All numbers come from one user split (seed 0). Differences of a few F1 points should be confirmed with the 'full' profile (3 held-out lists) before they are claimed.
